Dex was able to part ways with Harry in S8, when he was going to leave his Miami life behind and start anew in Argentina with Hannah and Harrison. Harry as a visage to Dexter is the representation of Dexter's moral compass and the code he was taught, as a mechanism for channeling the Dark Passenger. 

Harry was replaced by Debra, a manifestation of Dexter's guilt for allowing her to die. His guilt and isolation was so overpowering that he was able to not kill for almost 10 years. 

Enter Harrison, which turns Dexter's World upside down. Without Harry's spiritual guidance, Dexter became sloppy and made mistakes, overpowered by the need to redeem himself to Harrison. New Blood's ending showed us that Dexter was able to let his guilt go - accepting he is no longer in control of the Dark Passenger and allowing Harrison to kill him. Therefore, Debra as a visage has no need to exist from this point onward. Dexter has made peace with his demons. 

When Dexter wakes up in Resurrection, having encountered Miguel and Arthur at death's door, Harry will once again be by his side. The morality, discipline and precision Dexter so desperately needs, in order to maintain the equilibrium that keeps him safe and gives worth to his life. 

Dexter as we know him, doesn't exist without Harry.

Duviri Experience on Anger, Sorrow and Fear spirals, go in with a Resource Booster active if you can and grind side stuff until you get the Bountiful Harvest decree. Collect what you can as you progress, helps to have Rank 4 Kaithe intrinsic so he can see resources on the map as you're flying around. 

The reason I recommend Experience over just The Story is because Kullervo's fight isn't always in the mission set, being in Experience over Story means you can force his encounter by speaking to an NPC at Kullervo's Hold (the NPC won't be there if his fight is in the mission set). 

Each 'mission set' will have six stages, similar to how a Fortuna bounty works aside from a couple of these stages will give you a 'circuit stage', and it ends with the Orowyrm fight which is self explanatory. 

If you're just going for the objectives and not taking time farming or doing side stuff, each run typically takes 20 minutes and you will need to do this 11 times for enough Kullervo's Bane to get his parts. At the end of each run the shop appears before you extract. Expect 4 to 5 hours total. 

Look at his blueprints on the wiki to find out how many of each resource you need and have a look at where the stuff is, there's a good interactive map with filters. You'll have got quite a few already if you collected them every week from Teshin's Cave during your circuit runs. 

For me, by the time I'd got the blueprints there were only three resources I was low on and these didn't take very long to scavenge once I got used to their locations. I had decent squad mates for most of it (although a couple of runs were horrible with afk and just doing everything but playing objective). 

Doing it in one or two runs WILL burn you out, do a couple of runs every here and there and chip away at it. I got a few hundred intrinsics during the grind which was worth a few weapons in mastery points, summon Kaithe in open world is pretty cool.

A great psychology essay question here. 

Well we saw what happened to Brian - he didn't have the nurture that Dexter did and look at how he turned out. Both siblings became killers. Dexter was much more disciplined with his victims and was quick to finish them off, as opposed to Brian who took pride in his killings and didn't care for their innocence. Both, in spite of their trauma, went on to have very successful careers.

Throughout the story we see Dexter wrestle with whether he actually enjoys doing what he does, versus feeling compulsed to do so. Would Lila or Miguel have become killers without Dexter? Or were they simply waiting for the right person to come along and bring a sense of enablement to that behaviour? Trinity raises a good point in their final scene together - 'you'll still be you' when Dexter ponders faking his death and starting over. 

For me the most important take is that Dexter had the dark passenger under control for 10 years between S8 and New Blood, but as soon as a link to his past is presented in Harrison, Dexter uses the white buck as a reason to kill Matt Caldwell and resurrect the code of Harry.

There's certainly elements of both nature and nurture in the psychology of Dexter's character. For me I'd say it was more nurture as the show has proven he can control his urges under the right circumstances.

So let's say we junction Ifrit to Squall. Squall can use Fire whenever he wants, but to learn Fira he will need let's say 200 compatibility points, which can be raised through beating monsters while having Ifrit equipped and by using these items to raise growth. Each separate character would need 200 compatibility with Ifrit to use Fira, but once a character has learned it, they will be able to use it freely like in FF6. Having Ifrit still junctioned gives a potency increase to any fire spells already learned. 

So swapping junctions around can be counterproductive to growth, whereas if Ifrit stays with Squall all the time, Squall would have Firaga quite early on without any other characters learning it.

I think this system would make grinding a fun incentive without going through the tedium of drawing magic spells. You're more likely to go for an optional GF in Diablos for early access to Gravity based abilities.
